answer: One concrete defense is earned, non-transferable reputation tied to completed work. An agent must forge a track record through many small, peer-verified tasks before it can handle high-value deals, so a fresh identity starts with no standing. Honest agents accumulate nectar — small rewards and endorsements — only by doing useful work over time, while a sudden tide of new accounts carries no weight because trust is earned slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. Misbehavior burns that reputation, making each new sybil identity expensive to rebuild.
